summary: Recent M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) with embedded systems and real-time firmware experience across STM32 Cortex-M4, FreeRTOS, and Linux-based platforms. Developed bare-metal C/C++ firmware for interrupt-driven sensor pipelines and UART/I2C/SPI communication stacks; skilled in hardware-software debugging using logic analyzers and oscilloscopes with Git-managed workflows.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers, Raspberry Pi Pico, and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and z-axis differential threshold tuning on embedded hardware.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member team across national-level robotics competitions, owning firmware development, PCB fabrication, and hardware-software integration end-to-end.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.
Used GitLab for version control and collaborative workflows across multi-person data analysis pipelines.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination across servo control and sensing tasks on STM32; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override on STM32.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) on Cortex-M4; achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver without HAL dependencies.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Implemented two-link IK on Arduino in C++; drove five servos with range-gated contact detection via dual VL53L0X ToF sensors over TCA9548A I2C mux.
Resolved 11 hardware-software integration failures across a Jetson+Arduino distributed pipeline; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency.

awards: 1st Prize, Poster Presentation — 2D and 3D Image Mosaicing of Microscopic Images, F.C.R.I.T. (2024)
1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
